Parse MetaRVM Configuration File

Source: R/parse_config.R
parse_config.Rd

Reads and parses a YAML configuration file for MetaRVM simulations, extracting all necessary parameters for epidemic modeling including population data, disease parameters, mixing matrices, vaccination schedules, and simulation settings.

Usage

parse_config(config_file, return_object = FALSE)

Arguments

config_file

Character string. Path to a YAML configuration file containing model parameters and settings.

return_object

Logical. If TRUE, returns a MetaRVMConfig object for method chaining and enhanced functionality. If FALSE (default), returns a named list for backward compatibility.

Value

If return_object = FALSE (default), returns a named list containing entries common to both diseases plus disease-specific initial compartments and parameter matrices:

disease

The resolved disease name ("flu" or "measles")

N_pop

Number of population groups

pop_map

Data.table with population_id and user-defined demographic categories

Initial compartments

For flu: S_ini, E_ini, I_asymp_ini, I_presymp_ini, I_symp_ini, H_ini, D_ini, V_ini, R_ini. For measles: S_ini, E1_ini, E2_ini, I1_Q_ini, I1_U_ini, I2_Q_ini, I2_U_ini, R_ini, V1_ini, V2_ini plus the vaccinated-breakthrough compartment initials.

vac_time_id, vac_counts, vac_mat

Vaccination schedule data (flu only; not present for measles, which instead folds vaccination into the initial V1_ini/V2_ini compartments)

m_wd_d, m_wd_n, m_we_d, m_we_n

Contact mixing matrices

Disease parameter matrices (nsim × N_pop)

For flu: ts, ve, dv, de, dp, da, ds, dh, dr, pea, psr, phr. For measles: beta, de1, de2, di1, di2, prop_I1_Q, prop_I2_Q, V1_eff, V2_eff.

start_date

Simulation start date as Date object

sim_length

Simulation length in days

nsim

Number of simulation instances

nrep

Number of stochastic replicates per parameter set

random_seed

Random seed used (auto-generated if not supplied)

delta_t

Time step size (fixed at 0.5)

chk_file_names, chk_time_steps, do_chk

Checkpointing configuration

If return_object = TRUE, returns a MetaRVMConfig object with methods for parameter access and validation.

Details

The function processes a YAML configuration file with the following main sections:

Model Selection:

  • model.disease: Required. Selects the disease to simulate; supported values are "flu" and "measles". The disease choice determines which disease parameters are expected, the population initialization CSV column schema, and whether a vaccination schedule file is used (flu only; see below).

Simulation Configuration:

  • random_seed: Optional random seed for reproducibility in case of stochastic simulations or stochastic parameters

  • nsim: Number of simulation instances (default: 1)

  • nrep: Number of stochastic replicates per parameter set (default: 1) #'

  • start_date: Simulation start date in MM/DD/YYYY format

  • length: Simulation length in days

  • checkpoint_dir: Optional checkpoint directory for saving intermediate results

  • checkpoint_dates: Optional list of dates to save checkpoints.

  • restore_from: Optional path to restore simulation from checkpoint

Population Data: The required initialization CSV columns are disease-specific; any additional columns are treated as demographic categories.

  • Flu: population_id, N, S0, I0, V0, R0 (optional: E0, Ia0, Ip0, H0, D0, defaulted to 0 when absent).

  • Measles: population_id, N, S0, and at least one of I1_U0, I2_U0 (optional: E10, E20, I1_Q0, I2_Q0, R0, V10, V20, and the vaccinated-breakthrough compartment columns, all defaulted to 0 when absent). Measles has no I0 column.

  • vaccination: CSV file with a time-varying vaccination schedule. Flu only — the first column must be dates in MM/DD/YYYY format, and the rest of the columns must correspond to respective subpopulations in the numeric order of population_id. Measles vaccination is specified instead via the initial V10/V20 compartment counts in the initialization file; no separate vaccination file is used.

Mixing Matrices: Contact matrices for different time periods. Each CSV file must have a matrix of order (N_pop x N_pop), where, N_pop is the number of subpopulations. It is assumed that the i-th row and j-th column correspond to i-th and j-th subpopulations.

  • weekday_day, weekday_night: Weekday contact patterns

  • weekend_day, weekend_night: Weekend contact patterns

Disease Parameters: Epidemiological parameters (can be scalars or distributions). The exact parameter names are disease-specific:

  • Flu: ts, ve, dv, de, dp, da, ds, dh, dr, pea, psr, phr

  • Measles: beta, de1, de2, di1, di2, prop_I1_Q, prop_I2_Q, V1_eff, V2_eff

Sub-population Parameters: sub_disease_params allows specification of different parameter values for specific demographic categories (e.g., age groups, races).

The function supports stochastic parameters through distribution specifications with dist, mu, sd, shape, rate, etc.

Parameter Distributions

Disease parameters can be specified as distributions for stochastic modeling:

  • lognormal: dist: "lognormal", mu: value, sd: value

  • gamma: dist: "gamma", shape: value, rate: value

  • uniform: dist: "uniform", min: value, max: value

  • beta: dist: "beta", shape1: value, shape2: value

  • gaussian: dist: "gaussian", mean: value, sd: value

File Requirements

Population initialization file must contain columns (see Population Data above for the full disease-specific list):

  • population_id: Unique identifier for each population group, natural numbers

  • N: Total population size of the subpopulation

  • Flu: S0, I0, V0, R0

  • Measles: S0, and at least one of I1_U0, I2_U0

  • Optional user-defined category columns (e.g., age, race, zone, income_level, occupation)

Vaccination file (flu only) must contain: date (MM/DD/YYYY format) and vaccination counts for each population group. Not used for measles.

See also

metaRVM for running simulations with parsed configuration MetaRVMConfig for the configuration object class process_vac_data for vaccination data processing

Arindam Fadikar

Examples

# \donttest{
options(odin.verbose = FALSE)
example_config <- system.file("extdata", "example_config.yaml", package = "MetaRVM")
# Parse configuration file and return list (backward compatible)
config <- parse_config(example_config)

# Parse and return MetaRVMConfig object for method chaining
config_obj <- parse_config(example_config, return_object = TRUE)

# Access parameters from config object
config_obj$get("N_pop")
#> [1] 24
config_obj$list_parameters()
#>  [1] "N_pop"                  "disease"                "pop_map"               
#>  [4] "category_names"         "S_ini"                  "E_ini"                 
#>  [7] "I_asymp_ini"            "I_presymp_ini"          "I_symp_ini"            
#> [10] "H_ini"                  "D_ini"                  "P_ini"                 
#> [13] "V_ini"                  "R_ini"                  "vac_time_id"           
#> [16] "vac_counts"             "vac_mat"                "m_wd_d"                
#> [19] "m_wd_n"                 "m_we_d"                 "m_we_n"                
#> [22] "start_date"             "sim_length"             "nsim"                  
#> [25] "nrep"                   "random_seed"            "parallel"              
#> [28] "verbose"                "suppress_odin_messages" "delta_t"               
#> [31] "chk_file_names"         "chk_time_steps"         "do_chk"                
#> [34] "ts"                     "ve"                     "dv"                    
#> [37] "de"                     "dp"                     "da"                    
#> [40] "ds"                     "dh"                     "dr"                    
#> [43] "pea"                    "psr"                    "phr"                   

# Use with MetaRVM simulation
results <- metaRVM(config_obj)
# }
